task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED this design at BLOCKER severity -- read its full result.summary in handoffs/WF03-ISS0400-20260901/step-02b-code-design-validator.json before changing anything. In one sentence: resolve_nested_split/3 as specified in your prior design (§2.3) resets index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index before folding over the nested split's own branches, but that reset is only safe between TOP-LEVEL find_matching_join/2 branches (where a call's own stack is always fully unwound before returning, per ISS-0398 design §2.2.3) -- resolve_nested_split/3 instead fires MID-FLIGHT, from inside an already-open outer-walk call frame (the node leading into the nested split, e.g. A, has not returned), so wiping stack_set at that point destroys live back-edge detection for that still-in-progress ancestor. The validator constructed a concrete counterexample (outer_split -> A -> inner_split, with one inner branch looping back to A) and traced it step-by-step to a genuine infinite regress: A's back-edge to itself is no longer visible after the reset, so A is re-explored as fresh, re-recurses into inner_split, which re-triggers resolve_nested_split/3 again with another reset, forever. This also exposed an internal contradiction between design §2.3 (specifies a reset) and §3.3 (claims stack/stack_set are shared across the recursive boundary like memo is) -- the two describe incompatible algorithms; the validator's trace shows the reset (as literally specified) is what actually governs.

Your rework must design a genuinely different mechanism for detecting a live back-edge from inside a nested split's own fold back to an outer-walk ancestor -- the validator's own summary suggests one direction (do NOT reset stack/stack_set/index/lowlink at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary at all; only reset between find_matching_join/2's own TOP-LEVEL branches, where the unwound-stack proof actually applies; give each nested fold its own freshly-numbered index space that COMPOSES WITH, rather than replaces, the outer walk's live stack_set membership check) but you must design and re-prove it sound against this exact counterexample yourself, not merely re-assert the prior claim. Re-run your own worked trace against the validator's exact counterexample graph (outer_split -> A -> inner_split with the ia -> A back-edge, described in full in the validator's result.summary) and show explicitly, step by step, that the revised mechanism terminates and correctly detects the cycle. The validator's other findings (memo-key soundness for the non-cyclic case, the @max_nodes arithmetic, the zero-split-role-fixtures non-regression claim, the :dead_end propagation choice, and the absence of .ex bodies) were all independently verified SOUND and do not need to be redesigned -- only the stack/stack_set reset-vs-share mechanism at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary needs to change. On finishing, flip status to COMPLETED and write your own result block as normal -- this is not a first dispatch, so do not treat 'claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only' as still in force; the handoff is already claimed and this is a real rework with a real result expected.
acceptance_criteria: The revised design explicitly does NOT reset stack/stack_set/index/lowlink at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary in a way that destroys live back-edge detection for an outer-walk ancestor still on the call chain -- or uses some other mechanism that is explicitly proven not to, against the validator's exact counterexample

A step-by-step worked trace against the validator's own counterexample graph (outer_split -> A -> inner_split, inner branch looping back to A) is included, showing explicit termination and correct cycle detection under the revised mechanism
The revised design does not reintroduce the ISS-0398 memo-key-unsoundness defect class or the naive-visited-set-copy DoS defect class the validator confirmed were previously avoided
No .ex implementation bodies present in the design doc
Design doc explicitly reconciles or removes the prior §2.3/§3.3 internal contradiction the validator found

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 1 complete. Replaced iteration 1's resolve_nested_split/3 reset discipline (index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index reset before folding over the nested split's own branches) with full, unmodified state sharing at that boundary: resolve_nested_split/3 now threads the exact incoming leaf_search_state() -- all six fields, including stack/stack_set/index/lowlink/next_index -- through its own fold over the nested split's outgoing edges, exactly as an ordinary step-5 sibling-edge fold (fold_outgoing_edges/4) already threads state across any branching node's own children. reset_stack_bookkeeping/1 remains reserved exclusively for find_matching_join/2's own TOP-LEVEL per-branch reset (ISS-0398 design 2.2.3's unwound-stack proof, unchanged); resolve_nested_split/3 must never call it (design SS6 states this as an explicit ELIXIR-DEV invariant). Because stack_set is never wiped at this boundary, a live back-edge from inside a nested split's own branch into a still-open outer-walk ancestor is detected by the ordinary, unmodified step-2 on-stack check -- there is no nested-split-shaped blind spot left in the Tarjan machinery. Re-derived soundness with a full step-by-step trace against CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own exact counterexample graph (outer_split -> A -> inner_split, out_degree 2, split role; branch a: inner_split -> ia -> A closing the cycle; branch b: inner_split -> ib -> inner_join -> post -> outer_join) in design SS3.2: the walk visits A, inner_split, ia, ib, inner_join, post, outer_join each exactly once as a fresh exploration, resolve_nested_split/3 is entered exactly once (never re-entered), the back-edge ia->A is correctly detected on its first and only encounter via the unmodified step-2 check, the SCC {A, inner_split, ia} closes correctly at A (the true root, local_lowlink pulled to 0 by ia's back-edge), and the branch resolves to the correct singleton {:gateway,"outer_join"} -- explicit termination, no infinite regress. Reconciled the SS2.3/SS3.3 internal contradiction the validator found: both sections now describe the identical no-reset mechanism, with SS3.3 rewritten to distinguish a clean-closure dead-end verdict (unchanged from iteration 1) from an {:open, lowlink} propagation verdict (now explicitly the same step-5 propagation rule SS2.3 itself specifies, not a separately-asserted claim). SS3.4's termination argument, SS6's signature summary, and SS7's open questions updated to match. Replaced design SS4 fixture 3 (which exercised a different, non-matching cycle shape) with the validator's own exact counterexample graph as nested_split_ancestor_back_edge_graph/0 (positive case, resolves to {:ok,"outer_join"}, with an explicit non-regression assertion that the call completes at all in bounded time -- the direct regression check for the BLOCKER, since iteration 1's mechanism would never have returned on this fixture) plus nested_split_ancestor_back_edge_no_escape_graph/0 (fixture 3b, negative twin retaining the pure-cycle-no-escape coverage iteration 1's fixture 3 provided). Did not touch SS3.1 (memo-key soundness), SS3.4's @max_nodes arithmetic, the zero-split-role-fixtures claim, the :dead_end propagation choice for the clean-closure case, or fixtures 1/2/4 -- all independently verified sound by the validator and out of scope for this rework per the handoff's own instruction. No .ex implementation bodies added or present (only @spec/@type fences and prose, confirmed by direct re-read of the full file after editing).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-gate (WF-03 Step 2b recheck 1) against the revised resolve_nested_split/3 mechanism in lib/letflow/design/iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md.

Internal contradiction found between design section 2.3 (specifies reset) and section 3.3 (claims sharing). Full trace and all other independently-verified-sound findings recorded in handoffs/WF03-ISS0400-20260901/step-02b-code-design-validator.json.
issues: BLOCKER: resolve_nested_split/3 as specified never terminates on a legal graph shape where a nested split's own branch loops back to an ancestor still open on the outer walk's call chain.
